title: Algebraic Proof
standard_text: Argue mathematically to show algebraic expressions are equivalent, and use algebra to support and construct arguments and proofs.
meta_desc: Free Year 11 GCSE maths worksheets on algebraic proof: odd, even and multiples, consecutive numbers, expanding to prove, counterexamples and completing proofs. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Even = 2n, odd = 2n + 1, multiple of k = k × an integer.
key_sub: One counterexample proves a statement false.
body_html:
How it works

Write the numbers in algebra: an even number is 2n, an odd number is 2n + 1, consecutive integers are n, n + 1, n + 2. Expand and simplify, then take out a factor: 6n + 9 = 3(2n + 3) is a multiple of 3.

Checking a few numbers is not a proof. But one counterexample is enough to show a statement is false.

Example

Prove the sum of three consecutive integers is a multiple of 3.

n + (n + 1) + (n + 2) = 3n + 3

Answer: 3(n + 1)

Example

Show (n + 3)² − (n − 3)² is a multiple of 12.

n² + 6n + 9 − (n² − 6n + 9)

Answer: 12n

Common mistakes

  • Testing a few values and calling it a proof.
  • Using n and n for two different odd numbers.
  • Not taking out the factor at the end.

faq.q: How do you write an odd number in algebra?
faq.a: 2n + 1 (or 2n − 1), where n is an integer. 2n is always even, so 2n + 1 is always odd.
One example that makes a statement false. It is enough to disprove the statement.

items.q: Prove that the square of an odd number is odd: (2n + 9)² = 4n² + 36n + 81 = 2(…) + 1. What goes in the bracket?
items.e: Take out 2 from 4n² + 36n + 80 and leave the 1.

items.q: Expand and simplify (2n + 3)² − (2n − 3)².
Expand and simplify (n + 3)² − n(n + 1).
Expand and simplify (2n + 8)² − (2n − 8)².
Expand and simplify (n + 2)(n + 5) − n(n + 7).
items.e: (n² + 7n + 10) − (n² + 7n) = 10, the same for every n.

items.q: Expand and simplify (2n + 9)² + (2n + 3)².
items.e: Expand each bracket and collect: 8n² + 48n + 90. Every term but the last is even and the last is even too, so the sum of two odd squares is even.
